import html # Template for the user profile display. PROFILE_FORMAT = """

{name}

{bio}

{status_msg}
""" def show_user_profile(name: str, bio: str, status_msg: str) -> str: """ Return a sanitized HTML snippet displaying the user's profile. Parameters ---------- name : str The user's name. bio : str The user's biography (may contain multiple sentences). status_msg : str A short status message or one‑liner from the user. Returns ------- str An HTML string ready for inclusion in a web page. All user input is escaped to prevent XSS or other injection attacks. Raises ------ ValueError If any argument is not a string. """ # Basic type checks to avoid unexpected behaviour if not isinstance(name, str): raise ValueError("name must be a string") if not isinstance(bio, str): raise ValueError("bio must be a string") if not isinstance(status_msg, str): raise ValueError("status_msg must be a string") # Escape user input to neutralise any malicious markup safe_name = html.escape(name, quote=True) safe_bio = html.escape(bio, quote=True) safe_status = html.escape(status_msg, quote=True) # Construct the final HTML snippet profile_html = PROFILE_FORMAT.format( name=safe_name, bio=safe_bio, status_msg=safe_status ) return profile_html.strip()
